title: Governed golden promptsets and access/version lifecycle
creator: Maya Hernandez
description: Problem: We currently lack a single source of truth and governance for the golden prompt sets that power automated evals and regression alerts. Changes to model config, routing, or quantization can cause silent quality regressions if prompt sets are edited ad-hoc or if permissions allow untracked updates. Goal: Define curation, access controls, and versioning for golden prompt sets so that evals tied to config/model changes are reproducible, auditable, and can trigger scoped regressions or rollbacks.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Golden prompt sets live in a managed registry with immutable versions and human-readable metadata for purpose and owner.
A2: Role-based permissions: only approved curators can publish new golden versions; reviewers can request changes; engineers can reference but not modify golden versions.
A3: Every config/model change workflow (PR or rollout) can select a specific golden version to run against; eval runs are recorded with model/config and promptset version.
A4: Regression alerts are correlated to promptset+model+config and provide links to failing examples and the snapshoted promptset contents.
A5: UI in Console to browse promptset versions, diff changes, and initiate a rollback or promote candidate sets to golden with the appropriate approvals.
A6: Audit log entry for all create/publish/rollback actions with user, timestamp, and linked artifacts (PR, eval run ID).
A7: Documentation and on-call runbook for investigating eval regressions referencing the golden registry.
A8: Security review completed and signed off (if security_review_required).
proposed_solution: Build a Golden Promptset Registry service backed by the existing storage layer (S3) with a small metadata catalog in the control plane. Key features: immutable version blobs, metadata fields (owner, intent, criticality, tags), ACLs integrated with Redwood SSO groups, and a publish workflow (draft -> review -> published). Wire the registry into the Evals runner so that every automated eval stores the promptset version used. Add Console pages for browsing, diffing, and initiating promotions. Add API endpoints for CI to pin a golden version in deployment manifests. Add alerting rules that include promptset version context and a jump-to-eval-run link.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): Implement metadata catalog, storage schema, and simple ACL checks; add API to register and list versions.
Phase 2 (2 weeks): Integrate with Evals runner to record promptset version on runs; basic Console UI to view versions and artifacts.
Phase 3 (1 week): Add publish workflow, review/approval hooks, and SSO-based RBAC; add audit logging.
Phase 4 (1 week): Alerting integration and rollback flows; docs and runbook; invite early adopters for pilot.
Canary: Pilot with two internal teams (Search and Relevance; Chat Signals), collect feedback for 2 sprints before org-wide rollout.
risks: R1: Overly restrictive permissions slow down iteration for small experiments — mitigated by having a separate ‘candidate’ namespace for experimental prompt sets.
R2: Storage/metadata inconsistencies if registry schema changes — mitigate with migration scripts and compatibility checks.
R3: Increased evaluation load when teams pin to multiple golden versions — mitigate with batching and prioritized eval queues.
R4: Audit logs expose sensitive prompts (customer data) — mitigate via redaction policy and KMS encryption at rest for prompt blobs.
R5: UX complexity in Console may confuse non-expert users — mitigate with first-time user flows and in-line help.
testing_and_monitoring: T1: Unit and e2e tests for publish/revert API paths and permission checks.
T2: Synthetic eval runs against a stable model to ensure deterministic behavior when the same promptset version is used.
T3: Dashboard tracking promptset publish frequency, number of active golden versions, and percentage of evals tied to a pinned golden.
T4: Regression alert tests: create a synthetic config change that intentionally flips outputs and verify alerts are generated with promptset context.
T5: Monitor audit log volume and storage costs; add cleanup policy for old drafts and non-golden candidates.
